newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat postpones meeting with Israeli businesses.
newsitem.headline: Arafat postpones meeting with Israeli businesses.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat has postponed a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with Israeli businessmen on advancing economic ties, a spokeswoman for the Israeli group said on Tuesday.

The meeting had to be put off because of Arafat's sudden appointment with U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, said the spokeswoman for delegation head Benjamin Gaon, president and chief executive of Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's largest holding concern. No other date was set.
Gaon had said the meeting would demonstrate their commitment to peace and cementing relations with Palestinians.

The group was to include the chairmen of Israel's leading banks, the president and chief executive of Clal Israel Ltd David Wainshal, Israel Borovich, head of Arkia Israeli Airlines Ltd, and Michael Strauss, head of Nahariya Dairy Strauss Ltd.

Gaon openly supported the re-election campaign of Labour leader Shimon Peres, who was defeated in May by right-wing Likud leader Benjamin Netanyahu. But Gaon insisted the meeting was not a political statement.
Ross arrived in Cairo on Tuesday on a mission to revive Middle East peace talks. He will meet Arafat in Gaza and Netanyahu in Israel.
